source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), presentation deck "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles (SRI)], undated PowerPoint presentation (no author, date, or elibrary URL visible on slides)
text:
The System of Rice Intensification (SRI), called in Khmer "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវតាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" (rice cultivation system following natural principles), is a set of rice-growing techniques distinct from conventional rice cultivation. It was first developed in Madagascar in the 1980s by Henri de Laulanie.

In 1990, SRI began to spread to many other countries through promotion by CIIFAD (Cornell International Institute for Food, Agriculture and Development), with the involvement of the agricultural specialist Norman Uphoff. By the early 2000s the method had spread to 22 countries.

In Cambodia, SRI trials began in 1995, starting with a pilot group of 28 farming families. By 2005, the number of farmers practicing SRI in Cambodia had grown to approximately 40,000 farmers, farming in about 2,000 villages across 20 provinces and municipalities (khet-krong). These adoption figures are stated on the source slides without further breakdown by individual province.
